answer: PostgreSQL was chosen for the billing service because auditability mattered more than DynamoDB's lower migration effort. DynamoDB was tried for the billing prototype but the migration failed because conditional-update semantics did not match the existing transaction flow; Claude later confirmed the failure after reviewing integration-test output.

Redis caching was tested to reduce API latency. It was abandoned because the experiment increased cache invalidation complexity. It was later retried with a narrower cache scope, but the latency improvement was negligible.

The first invoice export attempt timed out after 18 minutes. Exports were then switched to asynchronous jobs. The first full customer batch subsequently completed successfully via the asynchronous approach.
